executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO covering late 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate epidemiological alerts in the Americas region with both November 2025 and March 2026 updates indicating sustained activity, representing a critical zoonotic threat with pandemic potential. The Southern Hemisphere influenza season commenced in April 2026 coinciding with ongoing RSV circulation, while mpox, dengue, chikungunya, measles, and pertussis all generated formal alerts indicating elevated multi-pathogen burden. Yellow fever activity in the Americas and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome further compound the regional risk profile.
bottomLine: The Americas face a high multi-pathogen burden in 2026 led by H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk, resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases, and escalating arboviral transmission concurrent with Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover events in the Americas with ongoing animal reservoir activity
Pandemic potential pathogen requiring continuous monitoring at human-animal interface
threats.action: Activate enhanced surveillance at human-animal interface, ensure H5N1 antiviral stockpiles are current, conduct risk assessments for exposed agricultural and wildlife workers, and coordinate with FAO and OIE on regional containment measures

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active transmission in the Americas
Ongoing clade-level monitoring required following 2024 global clade Ib emergence
Sustained community transmission risk in regions with low vaccination coverage
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs, ensure laboratory diagnostic capacity for clade differentiation, and issue clinical guidance updates to healthcare providers across the region

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating elevated dengue burden following record 2024 season
Hyperendemic multi-serotype circulation increasing severe dengue risk
Early 2026 reporting suggesting continuation of elevated transmission trends
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations particularly Aedes aegypti surveillance, enhance hospital capacity for severe dengue case management, and promote community-based larval source reduction campaigns

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alert April 27 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
January 2026 alert on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation indicating dual respiratory burden
December 2025 alert on Northern Hemisphere season start indicating year-round hemispheric transmission pressure
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination in Southern Hemisphere countries, strengthen hospital surge capacity for respiratory illness, and monitor for unusual influenza strain activity or severity signals

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating yellow fever activity in the Americas
Enzootic transmission risk with epizootics in non-human primates serving as warning signal
Gaps in vaccination coverage in at-risk populations in endemic zones
threats.action: Ensure vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers, investigate epizootic events in non-human primates as sentinel signals, and strengthen surveillance in border regions between endemic and non-endemic areas

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained pertussis resurgence
Global pattern of pertussis resurgence linked to waning immunity and potential pathogen adaptation
Increased risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised individuals
threats.action: Strengthen routine childhood immunization programs, implement Tdap booster campaigns for adolescents and adults including pregnant women, and enhance laboratory diagnostic capacity for Bordetella pertussis confirmation

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert February 3 2026 indicating measles cases in the Americas region
Risk of elimination status loss in countries with vaccination coverage gaps below 95% threshold
Importation risk from endemic regions remains high
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments, implement supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas, and strengthen case-based surveillance with laboratory confirmation for all suspected cases

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 indicating chikungunya activity
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika in Aedes aegypti endemic areas complicates clinical differentiation
Potential for local outbreaks in areas with competent vectors and susceptible populations
threats.action: Strengthen arboviral surveillance to differentiate chikungunya from dengue clinically and by laboratory testing, implement integrated vector management, and provide clinical guidance for managing chronic chikungunya arthropathy

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is classified as a BSL-3 select agent and potential pandemic pathogen. Two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) document sustained H5N1 activity in the Americas region. This pathogen is of highest concern due to its pandemic potential, documented zoonotic spillover capability, and high case fatality rate in human infections. Enhanced biosafety protocols, PPE guidance for exposed workers, and coordination with BSL-3 laboratory networks for diagnostic confirmation are strongly recommended. No BSL-4 pathogen detections were identified in the reviewed reports.

diseases: Communicable disease threats (ECDC Week 16-20 2026 - multiple pathogens under surveillance)

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance remains a concern in the context of treatment failures during resurgence events
Influenza antiviral resistance monitoring warranted given sustained H5N1 and seasonal influenza co-circulation
ECDC weekly threat reports likely include AMR surveillance signals for Europe though specific data not available in report titles
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen burden in the Americas in early 2026 straining surveillance and response capacity across health systems
Sustained H5N1 activity across two consecutive surveillance periods (November 2025 and March 2026) suggests persistent enzootic establishment in the Americas
Resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) concurrent with arboviral escalation indicates compounding immunization and vector control gaps
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset in April 2026 overlapping with ongoing RSV circulation creates dual respiratory burden risk for healthcare systems
PAHO issuance of alert on GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse signals emerging non-communicable pharmacovigilance concerns intersecting with health system capacity
